segments.narration: Six weeks into the engagement, NorthRiver's steering committee meets to review your recommendations.
Sarah Chen, the CFO, points at the list. Why the contract tool, and not the leads agent?
This is where most engagement reports fail. Their recommendations trace back to nothing, so the only answer is that it seemed like a good idea.
Now the same question, answered from a card. Behind the contract tool is a pain: two contracts renewed by themselves, and one of them cost forty thousand dollars.
Behind the pain is Robert Pak, the person who feels it, his own words, and the interview where he said them, with its date.
Every pain becomes a card. No exceptions. From here on you run the math. Don't let the math forget the value.

segments.narration: Marcus Holloway runs property operations at NorthRiver. He has been there since year two.
A building in Boston lost its heating. The heating vendor had been booked by two regions at once.
Each region books from its own list. The vendor list lives in three systems that don't talk to each other, plus an Excel file, and the same vendor is listed differently in each.
The tenants went without heat, and NorthRiver refunded forty units of rent.
An audit had already flagged six inconsistencies in the vendor master. And the Northeast? Anita, the regional manager, keeps it in her head. She is close to retirement.

script.text: Before a card goes anywhere, someone has to be allowed to build it. That is governance, and every client has four corners of it.
Four corners. Where do we start?
In some companies anyone can build an assistant over a weekend. In others only IT may. Your card has to fit that rule.
If the tool on your card is not on the approved list, add the approval time to your plan. At NorthRiver, Lin's AI policy is still in legal review, so nothing is approved yet.
So the tool question waits on legal.
When every department sends its own AI requests, the same idea gets built three times. One place should collect them, and your cards go there.
Name who approves a card before it ships: security, legal, the sponsor. If nobody can, that is a finding too.
Is that the whole of governance?
No. Modules 3 and 6 go deeper. For now, check the four corners for every card, and write down what you do not know.
